set.body:
From the traceability ruling bd-01M166XWESBS1JZ5B38H0ZZ2DK, post-01M16KFZHZAACFWXTM3XCQS6N6.

RecallUnit carries both span: SpanSet and text: String (recall/unit.scala:126-128). RecallGraph.validated (graph.scala:34) checks only that spans fit inside the transcript and never that text equals the transcript at that span. Demonstrated: a unit with the span for 'First thing happened.' and the text 'THE GHOSTS WERE ANGRY...' validates clean.

Why it matters: 'which words support this cell' has two available answers - the span resolved against the transcript, and unit.text - with no law that they agree. The only code that turns a recall unit into a vector reads TEXT (embed-bench/channels.scala:126); a span-based trace answers with the TRANSCRIPT. AlignWire.recallChecksum commits to both (wire.scala:207-213), so it faithfully identifies an incoherent graph and never refuses one: identity is not validity.

Measured before proposing: with the check installed, recall 37 + align 177 + fixtures 110 = 324 tests pass, and the check was verified to discriminate (honest graph accepted, lying graph refused) rather than silently never firing. The invariant already holds in practice; enforcing it costs nothing today and closes it before the portable cell-trace function is built on the loose version.

Scope: RecallGraph.validated plus its suite. Not a behaviour change to any currently-passing input.
